extracted.intended_audience: attorneys authorized to practice before the USPTO (especially in trademark/non-patent matters), Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, disciplinary counsel, and respondents in USPTO reciprocal-discipline proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Official USPTO final order implementing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24: explains grounds for imposing identical discipline based on a state suspension, procedural requirements (notice/service/response), publication/notification duties, and the specific professional-rule violations that supported the state discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline identical to discipline imposed by a duly constituted authority of a State pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director of OED may file a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline and the USPTO may impose discipline identical to the state order; respondent is provided an opportunity to respond within the time prescribed by the regulation (40 days in this matter) and may oppose imposition for reasons listed in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) (state suspension predicate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) is predicated upon being suspended from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A state-imposed suspension can serve as the basis for suspension from practice before the USPTO in trademark and other non-patent matters; the USPTO order here suspends respondent for one year and one day based on that predicate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and service requirements (certified mail; opportunity to respond)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice and Order pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 must be sent to the respondent (here, by certified mail) and provide the respondent an opportunity to file a response opposing reciprocal discipline within the regulatory time period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case the Notice and Order was sent by certified mail (receipt nos. provided), delivered October 25, 2023, and explicitly afforded a 40-day response period; failure to timely respond is material to the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond — no genuine issue of material fact (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a respondent fails to file a response to the Notice and Order, the Office may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and impose reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order recites that respondent did not file a response and therefore the Office determined there was no genuine issue of material fact and imposed suspension identical to the state discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order in OED FOIA Reading Room
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room (http://foiadocuments.uspto.gov).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary decisions are made publicly available via the OED FOIA Reading Room; the order directs OED to publish the Final Order there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette notice content and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided 'Notice of Suspension' text describing the respondent, the suspension period, the rule violated (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)), and a summary of the underlying misconduct and state discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order supplies model language for the Official Gazette notice, including factual background (e.g., appearing while administratively suspended, holding oneself out as admitted, failure to notify clients, failure to appear in court) and the regulatory basis for action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for it to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where respondent is admitted and to courts where respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order directs dissemination of the discipline to relevant state agencies and courts to ensure notice beyond the USPTO records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order requires respondent to fulfill any continuing obligations under 11.58 (e.g., duties relating to communications, client notifications, other post-discipline duties) as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pennsylvania Rules of Professional Conduct 1.1 (competence)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Joint Petition provided that Ms. McPherson violated Pennsylvania Rules of Professional Conduct 1.1 (competence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of conduct supporting this violation in this matter include appearing as counsel while administratively suspended and failing to provide competent representation (e.g., failure to appear leading to adverse consequences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pennsylvania Rules of Professional Conduct 1.3 (diligence)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Joint Petition provided that Ms. McPherson violated Pennsylvania Rules of Professional Conduct 1.3 (diligence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order cites failure to diligently represent a criminal defendant by failing to appear for a scheduled hearing, resulting in a bench warrant and pretrial detention, as conduct demonstrating lack of diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pennsylvania Rules of Professional Conduct 5.5(a) (unauthorized practice of law)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Joint Petition provided that Ms. McPherson violated Pennsylvania Rules of Professional Conduct 5.5(a) (unauthorized practice of law).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appearing as counsel while administratively suspended constitutes unauthorized practice of law under the cited rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pennsylvania Rules of Professional Conduct 5.5(b)(1) (failure to maintain continuous presence)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Joint Petition provided that Ms. McPherson violated Pennsylvania Rules of Professional Conduct 5.5(b)(1) (failure to maintain a continuous presence within the jurisdiction for the practice of law).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order cites holding oneself out as admitted while administratively suspended as activity running afoul of this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pennsylvania Rules of Professional Conduct 5.5(b)(2) (improperly holding oneself out as admitted)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Joint Petition provided that Ms. McPherson violated Pennsylvania Rules of Professional Conduct 5.5(b)(2) (improperly holding oneself out as admitted to practice law in the jurisdiction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order notes that respondent held herself out as an attorney admitted to practice in Pennsylvania and D.C. while administratively suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pennsylvania Rules of Professional Conduct 7.1 (false or misleading communications)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Joint Petition provided that Ms. McPherson violated Pennsylvania Rules of Professional Conduct 7.1 (making a false or misleading communication regarding the lawyer or lawyer's services).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holding oneself out as authorized to practice while suspended is cited as an example of a false or misleading communication about legal status/services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pennsylvania Rules of Professional Conduct 8.4(c) (dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Joint Petition provided that Ms. McPherson violated Pennsylvania Rules of Professional Conduct 8.4(c) (conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order treats misrepresentations about admission status and related conduct as falling within this prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pennsylvania Rules of Professional Conduct 8.4(d) (conduct prejudicial to administration of justice)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Joint Petition provided that Ms. McPherson violated Pennsylvania Rules of Professional Conduct 8.4(d) (conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to appear for scheduled hearings and causing bench warrants/pretrial detention are cited as conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pennsylvania Rules of Disciplinary Enforcement 203(6)(3) (willful violation grounds for discipline)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Joint Petition provided that Ms. McPherson violated Pennsylvania Rules of Disciplinary Enforcement 203(6)(3) (willful violation of any provision of the Rules of Disciplinary Enforcement is grounds for discipline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The state disciplinary proceeding found willful violations of enforcement provisions, which supported the recommended suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pennsylvania Rules of Disciplinary Enforcement 217(b) (notify clients of suspension)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Joint Petition provided that Ms. McPherson violated Pennsylvania Rules of Disciplinary Enforcement 217(b) (requiring suspended attorneys to promptly notify clients of the suspension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order notes respondent failed to notify clients of her administrative suspension as required by this Enforcement rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pennsylvania Rules of Disciplinary Enforcement 217(d)(2) (cease communications conveying eligibility to practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Joint Petition provided that Ms. McPherson violated Pennsylvania Rules of Disciplinary Enforcement 217(d)(2) (requiring suspended attorneys to promptly cease and desist any communications which expressly or implicitly convey eligibility to practice law).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent's continued communications holding herself out as admitted while suspended are identified as violations of this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pennsylvania Rules of Disciplinary Enforcement 217(e)(1) (timely file verified statement of compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Joint Petition provided that Ms. McPherson violated Pennsylvania Rules of Disciplinary Enforcement 217(e)(1) (requiring suspended attorneys to timely file a verified statement attesting to their compliance with the provisions of the Enforcement rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely file required verified statements after suspension was relied upon in the state discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pennsylvania Rules of Disciplinary Enforcement 217(j)(1) (conduct law-related activities under supervision)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Joint Petition provided that Ms. McPherson violated Pennsylvania Rules of Disciplinary Enforcement 217(j)(1) (requiring suspended attorneys to conduct all law-related activities under the supervision of an attorney in good standing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engaging in law-related activities while suspended without proper supervision was cited as improper conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pennsylvania Rules of Disciplinary Enforcement 217(o)(4) (prohibition on engaging in law-related activities while suspended)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Joint Petition provided that Ms. McPherson violated Pennsylvania Rules of Disciplinary Enforcement 217(o)(4) (prohibiting suspended attorneys from otherwise engaging in any law-related activities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The state finding included that respondent engaged in law-related activities while administratively suspended, triggering this Enforcement prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Petition in Support of Discipline as basis for recommended sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent and the Pennsylvania Office of Disciplinary Counsel submitted a Joint Petition in Support of Discipline providing the factual and legal basis for recommending suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A joint recommendation between respondent and state disciplinary counsel may be presented to the USPTO as part of the record supporting the identical discipline; here the Joint Petition resulted in a state suspension of one year and one day and was noted by USPTO.
